summary: Phase 4 Slice F (onboarding router dual-write Mongo + Supabase Postgres) verified GREEN end-to-end. Backend pytest: 31/31 PASS in test_iteration15_phase4f_onboarding_dualwrite.py. Direct asyncpg + motor probes confirm: (1) POST /api/onboarding (admin) creates a step with id/caregiver_id/title/description/completed=false/completed_at=null and the row is mirrored exactly to BOTH public.onboarding (PG) and the Mongo onboarding collection; caregiver POST is forbidden (403). (2) GET /api/onboarding?caregiver_id=<uuid> as admin returns rows sourced from Postgres only — len == PG count for that caregiver_id and every record's caregiver_id matches the filter. (3) GET /api/onboarding as caregiver IGNORES the client-supplied caregiver_id query and forces caregiver_id=identity server-side — even when called with ?caregiver_id=<ADMIN_UUID> every returned step belongs to the demo caregiver, and len == PG count for the demo caregiver. (4) POST /api/onboarding/{id}/toggle: first toggle flips completed=true and sets completed_at to a non-null ISO timestamp in BOTH stores; second toggle flips back to completed=false and completed_at=null in BOTH stores; caregiver can toggle OWN step (200) but cannot toggle another caregiver's step (403); toggling a non-existent id returns 404. (5) DELETE /api/onboarding/{id} as admin removes the row from BOTH PG and Mongo; caregiver DELETE is rejected (403) and the row remains intact in BOTH stores. (6) POST /api/onboarding/bulk-assign for the demo caregiver (already migrated) returns created=0 on the first call AND on re-runs (idempotent); the endpoint is admin-only (caregiver receives 403); unknown caregiver_id returns 404. (7) Phase 4 Slice A/B/C/D/E regression GREEN under BOTH legacy HS256 (Admin@123) and Supabase ES256 (AdminPassword123!) JWTs: /auth/me, /caregivers, /clients (list+detail), /assignments, /documents, /shifts, /chat/threads, /chat/contacts — all 200 with expected shapes. (8) Final parity restored to baseline 52==52: PG onboarding=52 and Mongo onboarding=52 after cleanup; per-caregiver demo (CAREGIVER_UUID) PG=27 == Mongo=27 — exact match. Frontend regression (Expo web, mobile viewport 390x844): caregiver login (legacy mode) lands on Dashboard (1 Client / 12 Caregivers / 50 Documents; AUDIT READINESS 50%); bottom-nav Team -> 'My Onboarding' pill renders 27 steps from PG (cross-verified via /api/onboarding fetch with userToken: total=27, completed=0); tapping the first step's title row triggers POST /api/onboarding/{id}/toggle and the GET refresh confirms completed=true with completed_at='2026-06-26T15:22:44.534+00:00'; second tap restores completed=false / completed_at=null — toggle is bi-directional and persists. Documents and Schedule tabs load fine after the toggle flow. Admin login (Supabase mode) -> Dashboard renders OVERVIEW + 'Onboarding tasks 51 steps pending' (52 total, 1 completed) -> Team>Onboarding pill displays 52 step rows ('Review and sign:' occurs 52x in the DOM, matching PG count exactly). Direct navigation to /caregiver/389b257d-7edb-4d12-adfc-3b8e80f91bf1 renders 'Sarah Johnson' header with '1/27 onboarding · 1 clients · 0 credentials' summary and tabs 'Schedule (3) / Clients (1) / Creds (0) / Onboarding (27)' — the per-caregiver count 27 comes from the Postgres-sourced list. No expo/react-native deprecation issues or red-screen errors introduced by Slice F. The /api/onboarding read path round-trips through supa_data.list_onboarding_steps with a single SELECT (no Mongo fallback) and is materially simpler than the prior Mongo find-with-sort.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1213-1220 — POST /api/onboarding dual-writes Mongo first then PG via supa_data.upsert_onboarding_step. Since supa_data uses _safe() that swallows PG errors, if Mongo succeeds and PG fails, the API returns 200 to the client but the row is missing from PG. For Slice F this is acceptable best-effort behavior, but Slice J (Mongo decommission) must make PG authoritative and surface PG failures as 5xx.

server.py:1234-1248 — toggle_step reads the existing doc from Mongo (not PG) to compute the next completed/completed_at, and to do the 403 caregiver-owner check. If Mongo and PG drift, the PG row could be updated based on stale Mongo state. Tolerable while dual-write invariants hold, but the read should switch to PG (mirror the list_steps pattern) before Mongo is decommissioned.

server.py:1263-1295 — bulk_assign loops per-step with two awaits per iteration (Mongo insert_one + supa upsert). For the standard 14 caregiver_onboarding documents this is fine (28 round-trips). If the document set ever grows past ~50, consider a batched executemany on the PG side and an asyncio.gather over the loop body. Idempotency relies on the Mongo `{caregiver_id, title}` lookup — that index is implicit; recommend creating a compound unique index on (caregiver_id, title) to enforce idempotency at the DB level.

supa_data.py:811-827 — upsert_onboarding_step uses 'on conflict (id) do update set title=...description=...completed=...completed_at=...' which silently overwrites a PG-edited row with whatever Mongo's payload happens to contain. If a future direct PG write happens (e.g., Postgres trigger) it will be clobbered on the next API write. Safe today (no such triggers) but worth flagging.

supa_data.py:850-875 — list_onboarding_steps formats completed_at/created_at with to_char which emits '+00:00' as a literal string suffix; this works for the OnboardingStep pydantic model because the field is a plain str, but if the schema ever moves to datetime the suffix will need adjustment.

Frontend: caregiver detail page caregiver/[id].tsx onboarding tab is read-only (no onPress to toggle) — caregivers can only toggle from the Team -> 'My Onboarding' tab, which works. This is by design (admin viewing) but the visual checkbox affordance could be misleading to caregivers who land on the detail view. Not a Slice F regression.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 4 Slice F is GREEN. All onboarding endpoints are dual-write: POST/toggle/DELETE go to Mongo first, then PG via supa_data._safe wrapper. READS for GET /api/onboarding are entirely from Postgres (supa_data.list_onboarding_steps), with caregiver_id filter forced server-side when role='caregiver'. Bulk-assign is idempotent via Mongo {caregiver_id, title} lookup before each insert; each new step dual-writes. Permissions are unchanged from prior slices: create/delete/bulk-assign require admin; toggle requires owner-or-admin. Reusable fixtures in test_iteration15_phase4f_onboarding_dualwrite.py: legacy_admin_token, supabase_admin_token, legacy_caregiver_token, HA/HCG/HSUPA header fixtures; pg_fetchrow/pg_fetchval/pg_execute/pg_execute_fetch and mongo_count/mongo_find_one/mongo_delete sync helpers with event-loop-safe runner. Frontend testIDs verified: login-email-input, login-password-input, login-submit-button. The Onboarding row tap-to-toggle in (tabs)/team.tsx works via clicking the step title text (no dedicated testID exists yet — main agent may want to add `testID=onboarding-step-${item.id}` on the TouchableOpacity for more stable Playwright targeting, though current text-based selectors work). Next slice (per /app/scripts/) is presumably Slice G (policy_acks, client_tasks, training_completions, or packet_shares) or Slice J (Mongo decommission).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no failures during testing. The smoke test (_smoke_slice_f.py), the pytest suite (31/31), and the live frontend flow (caregiver legacy + admin Supabase) all passed on first run. Final parity exactly matches the documented baseline of 52 onboarding rows in both stores.
